clue.text: When arranged start to sell property

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
set means arranged or fixed in place

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here of sell

explanation.surface: An instruction to an estate agent: once everything is sorted, begin selling the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are possessions of value, the property a person or firm owns.

clue.text: Swear, visiting cricket match?

parts.note: to be visiting a place is to be at it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone cursing while watching a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a long international game of cricket, a sport much played in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare solemnly, as under oath, a sense of swear.

clue.text: Hand out two punishments in travel at rush hour?

parts.note: the strap is a beating with a leather belt, an old school punishment
the second punishment handed out is to hang, execution by the rope

explanation.surface: A judge dealing out a pair of sentences.
explanation.walkthrough: The strap is a leather beating once used in schools. Straphanging is standing on a crowded train or bus holding a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Commuters at peak times often have no seat and stand gripping an overhead strap, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Skating combination to upset S Coast resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the resort's name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Poole is a seaside town on England's south coast, in Dorset

explanation.surface: Something meant to annoy a seaside town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Poole is a resort town in Dorset on England's south coast; 'upset' turns it to ELOOP in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe loop is a figure-skating jump, the name combining two parts: a toe-pick takeoff and a loop.

clue.text: Snoopers going around to find poverty

indicators.note: the letters of snoopers go round and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Nosy investigators touring a neighbourhood to discover deprivation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' rearranges SNOOPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorness is the state of being poor, a synonym of poverty.

clue.text: Some common lynxes may be unique

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wildlife observation: a few ordinary wild cats could be one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ONLY from commON LYnxes.
explanation.definitionFit: An only child is a sole, unique one; the adjective means single, without equal.

clue.text: Downpour largely submerges old instrument cases

indicators.note: the trimmed rain closes over the instrument, holding it inside
most of the word for downpour, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: rain is a downpour
the viol is an early stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A storm soaks the boxes holding antique musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts RAIN to RAI, which 'submerges' VIOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels, cases wrapped round a filling.

clue.text: Acclaim part of index to list

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A librarian's note about a section of a list's index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes EXTOL from indEX TO List.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is what acclaim means as a verb.

clue.text: How not to enter this answer, perhaps rightly?

definitions.text: How not to enter this answer, perhaps rightly?

parts.words: How not to enter this answer, perhaps rightly
parts.note: this is a down light, so it must be entered top to bottom, not across the grid towards the right

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver asks which direction the answer should go in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a down entry; writing it from left to right, 'rightly', would be going across, the wrong way for this light.
explanation.definitionFit: Going across from left to right is moving laterally, at right angles to a down light's direction.

clue.text: Turn round Early English dish

indicators.note: turn goes round the abbreviation, holding it in the middle

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English, a style of Gothic architecture

explanation.surface: A cook rotates an old English serving bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Early English is a style of medieval Gothic architecture, abbreviated in reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep covered bowl for serving soup, a kind of dish.

clue.text: With the Spanish girl, boy is exhilarated

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
Eva is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is thrilled to be with a Spanish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated can mean in high spirits, elated or exhilarated.

clue.text: So-called swallow was a model

parts.note: to sup is to sip or swallow
a model posed for the artist

explanation.surface: Gossip: the alleged bird once sat for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed and so-called both describe something claimed but doubtful, as in 'the supposed expert'.

clue.text: Priest on team with Romeo's magic potion

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible's Book of Samuel
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
R is Romeo in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A cleric in a team alongside Shakespeare's lover, with his deadly potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is read down the grid: the priest sits above the team.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical or medicinal drink, supposedly giving long life.

clue.text: Grasp returning wolf that ate egg left

indicators.note: the reversed animal takes the egg and left inside it, as if swallowing them
returning means the word wolf is read backwards

parts.note: an egg is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hungry wolf comes back after eating an abandoned egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes WOLF into FLOW, which 'ate' O and L, giving F-OL-LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow an argument is to understand it, a sense of grasp.

clue.text: This flies — is a railway able to?

parts.note: can means is able (to)

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a train line can do something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a railway able to?' turned into a question gives 'can a railway', so CAN comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a small songbird, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Relevance of a very quiet pupil I initially chose with skill

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the music direction for very quiet
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of chose

parts.note: ability means skill

explanation.surface: A school report on a quiet pupil who chose a subject well.
explanation.definitionFit: Applicability is how far something applies, much the same as relevance.

clue.text: Noising it abroad will do for these firings

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of noising it are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Spreading the news will lead to dismissals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges NOISING IT. 'Firings' looks like sackings but means engines igniting.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine's ignitions are its firings, the moments the fuel is set alight.

clue.text: Estimated animals going to area around London died

parts.note: asses are donkeys, a kind of animal
SE, the South East, is the region of England around London
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Donkeys being driven to London's outskirts and dying, counted roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to judge its value or size, so assessed means estimated.

clue.text: Importance of indication providing one positive particle

parts.note: a sign is an indication
if means providing, as in 'providing it rains'
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cation is an ion with a positive charge

explanation.surface: A physicist explains why a single positively charged particle matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Signification is meaning or significance, close to importance.

clue.text: Journalist's announcement to produce a profound effect

parts.note: someone announcing who they are begins 'I'm'
the press is the trade of journalists, so a journalist's announcement ends with it

explanation.surface: A reporter introduces themselves, hoping to make a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: A journalist announcing themselves says 'I'm press'; the two words run together give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a deep mark on someone's mind or feelings is the verb's everyday sense.

clue.text: Pick up troublemaker going on ramble

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous creature or child
to rove is to wander or ramble

explanation.surface: A mischievous child setting off on a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Business or health that picks up gets better, the meaning of improve.

clue.text: Fruit not hot in these schools

indicators.note: not means the fruit is taken without the abbreviation for hot

parts.note: lychees are a sweet fruit from China
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Cold fruit being served in schools' canteens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from LYCHEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycées are French secondary schools.

clue.text: Key French art about keep fit

parts.note: in old English 'thou art' means you are, and the French for that is tu es
ca, short for circa, means about
PE is physical education, exercise to keep fit

explanation.surface: A vital point about French art and exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' here is the old form of are, as in 'thou art'; ES is the matching French verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape is a key on a computer keyboard, the one marked Esc.

clue.text: In these days corded cloth is different fabric

indicators.note: in puts the cloth inside the abbreviation for these days

parts.note: CE, the Common Era, is the present age
rep is a ribbed or corded fabric

explanation.surface: Fashion note: ribbed material is a distinct textile nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: REP goes 'In' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crêpe is a thin crinkled fabric, a cloth other than rep.

clue.text: My back route in outskirts of Salisbury gets agreement

indicators.note: in places the backwards my and the route between the outer letters
the outskirts of Salisbury are its first and last letters
back means the word my is read backwards

parts.note: a path is a route

explanation.surface: Someone's way home on the edge of a cathedral city meets approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MY into YM; YM and PATH go 'in' S and Y, the 'outskirts of' Salisbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy can mean agreement or accord, as in being in sympathy with a view.

clue.text: Practising philosopher's casual greeting with soldier

parts.note: yo is an informal hello
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A thinker greeting a soldier informally.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi practises yoga and Hindu philosophy, so is a philosopher in practice.

clue.text: Elks confused by school outline

indicators.note: the letters of elks are mixed up, as if confused

parts.note: Eton is a famous English private school

explanation.surface: Deer baffled by a school's plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes SKEL from ELKS; ETON is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a basic framework or sketch, as in a skeleton plan.

clue.text: Nothing in code gets one gloomy

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the name of the code

parts.note: Morse is the dots-and-dashes code
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Receiving a blank message makes a person depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes 'in' MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and bad-tempered, a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Article of clothing which could be resisted

indicators.note: could be says the letters of resisted can be made into something else

explanation.surface: A garment that someone might refuse to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges RESISTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress tie is a bow tie worn with evening dress, an item of formal wear.

clue.text: Old bit of vinyl aboard ship is rotting

indicators.note: aboard puts the record inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS is steamship
an EP is an old extended-play record

explanation.surface: An old record left on a vessel is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP, extended play, was a short vinyl record of a few tracks, popular in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepsis is infection and putrefaction in the body; 'rotting' is a loose noun-like sense of decay.
